page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e4.large is an x86_64 architecture virtual machine instance within the ecs.e4 family, running on the KVM hypervisor. It features 2 shared vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2682 v4 processor operating at 2.5 GHz, with 2 physical cores and 1.0 thread per core. The instance is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or bundled GPU hardware, and has a baseline network bandwidth of 0 Gbps with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates that the shared CPU allocation and older processor architecture limit overall performance. The instance scores in the bottom 10% for both single-core (945.88) and multi-core (1857.99) stress-ng CPU tests. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with large-block read-only and write speeds falling into the bottom 10% at 14.95 GB/sec and 11.46 GB/sec respectively, though small-block cached reads perform slightly better at 164.27 GB/sec. Database operations and static web serving throughput are similarly low, with Passmark database operations scoring 558.24 and static web serving throughput reaching 2.31 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.e4.large offers a high memory allocation relative to its compute resources, making it a budget-friendly option for memory-intensive workloads that do not require sustained high CPU performance. However, the shared CPU model and poor benchmark results across computational, cryptographic, and memory tests present a significant tradeoff. This instance is best suited for lightweight database caching, basic web serving with low traffic, or development and testing environments where memory capacity is prioritized over raw processing speed.
